dedupe_keys.name: bikedna bicycle infrastructure data and network quality assessment

description: BikeDNA (Bicycle Infrastructure Data and Network Assessment) is a tool for assessing, in a reproducible way, the quality of OpenStreetMap and other bicycle infrastructure data sets. It gives planners, researchers, data maintainers and cycling advocates an overview of data quality in an area, with a focus on fitness for purpose for network-based research and planning, including the topological structure of the bicycle network; positional accuracy is not directly evaluated. The analysis has three parts: an intrinsic analysis of OSM bicycle data, an intrinsic analysis of a non-OSM reference data set, and an extrinsic comparison of the two, followed by generated reports. It is described in a paper in Environment and Planning B, and a companion BikeDNA BIG handles large data sets. Coverage is any area the user chooses. Access: Jupyter notebooks in Python, free on GitHub under the GNU Affero General Public License version 3. Caveats: it highlights quality issues, not giving a final verdict, and the extrinsic part needs a reference data set. It supports the preparation of cycling networks for network flow and capacity planning models. It complements OSMnx, A/B Street and the PeopleForBikes network analysis catalogued here.
